- [2023/02/15] The Employee Retention Credit (ERC) is a refundable tax credit for businesses to keep employees on payroll during economic hardships like the COVID-19 pandemic.
- [2023/02/15] The ERC is available to employers who experienced a significant decline in gross receipts or were partially/fully suspended due to COVID-19 government orders.
- [2023/02/15] The ERC provides a credit equal to 70% of qualified wages, up to $10,000 per employee per quarter, with a maximum of $28,000 per employee for 2021.
- [2023/02/15] Eligibility for the ERC requires a decline in gross receipts of at least 20% in 2021 compared to the same quarter in 2019, or suspension due to COVID-19 orders.
- [2023/02/15] To claim the ERC, eligible employers must file Form 941 with the IRS.
- [2023/02/15] It is recommended that business owners consult with a tax professional to determine ERC eligibility and credit amount.
